quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Traffic only moves in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign tells drivers that traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if another car is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means that action is not allowed. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are prohibited.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water and puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid on quick turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When you park parallel to a curb, you must:

options.text: Park within 24 inches of the curb.
Park within 18 inches of the curb.
Park at an angle with your front facing out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park within 18 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking on a public road, park parallel to the curb and stay within 18 inches of it. Your car should face the same direction as traffic on your side of the road.

questions.question: What is the only way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to reduce your BAC is to stop drinking alcohol and let time pass. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers may help you stay awake, but they cannot lower your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: It begins to rain while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull onto the shoulder and stop until it clears up.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than normal traffic, jerking motions, and making quick sudden stops.

questions.question: Passing other vehicles is not allowed:
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass another vehicle on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When a stop sign controls the crossing.
When flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger tells you to, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.question: Which statement is true about passing?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure no cars are coming toward you.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Do not move back to your lane until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use turn signals when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This helps other drivers know your plans and prevents accidents.

questions.question: When should you try to notify the owner of another vehicle?

options.text: If you hit their vehicle while it is unattended.
If you don't like their bumper sticker.
If they are talking on their cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you hit their vehicle while it is unattended.
questions.explanation: You must try to find the owner of a vehicle you hit while they were not present. If you cannot find them, leave a note with your name, address, license plate number, and a description of the crash.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slick roads, slow down when taking turns and curves. Driving too fast on slippery surfaces is especially dangerous in turns.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.

questions.question: To drive safely, what should you do about your physical condition?

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular check-ups.
Know how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects how safely you can drive. Know your limitations and only drive if it is safe. Stay fit, know the effects of your medicine, and understand what your body can handle.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers when you are going to turn.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Steer straight and slowly remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slowly remove your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slowly lift your foot off the gas. Do not brake until you have control. Once stable, brake gently and pull to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Use turn signals whenever you move left or right. Signal when pulling into traffic from a parking space, moving to a new lane, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show that the road curves sharply in the direction the arrow points. In this case, the arrow points left. You may see several chevron signs placed throughout the curve.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:
questions.explanation: This sign means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign means pedestrians may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help reduce its effects?
questions.explanation: Only time allows the body to overcome the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: You see the driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Know that this driver is not paying attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving by talking to passengers, looking for things in your car, reading, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to crash.

questions.question: Which of these is a common cause of traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.explanation: Speeding for road conditions causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter and skateboard riders when the other lane is clear and it is safe.

questions.question: To change lanes safely, you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, use your turn signal and check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, slow down and move to the side to create space. Stop and wait. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left side.
Keep driving once you think the children have finished getting off.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move forward until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When other drivers around you are acting angry, you should:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, distance yourself from them. Do not make eye contact or use hand gestures. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever is safe to stay away from danger.

questions.question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous because you must take your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road. This makes it hard to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: The best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective action you can take to prevent death or injury while driving.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your ability to drive?

options.text: It makes you feel overly confident.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, harms your coordination, and weakens your vision and ability to judge distance.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Moving toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot any time you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, and moving toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are larger and heavier, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and stop unless you are already inside the intersection.
